messages.text:
Hello Support Team,
I’m having a persistent problem setting up Wi-Fi on my DC08. If I unplug Ethernet and try to set it up over Wi-Fi, I can see the miner’s setup network in my Wi-Fi list and connect to it. I then go to http://192.168.4.1, enter my home Wi-Fi information, save, and reboot.
After rebooting, the display returns to the setup screen with the QR codes. The W. settings I entered do not appear to have been saved, and the DC08 does not join my home Wi-Fi.
For comparison, my NerdQAxe connects to my Wi-Fi without a problem, and my BC04 works over both Wi-Fi and Ethernet. My home Wi-Fi is broadcast by two routers under the same network name.
Could you please advise the correct setup procedure and whether this may be a firmware issue? Please also let me know whether you recommend a reset, firmware update, or reflash, and what firmware details or screenshots would help troubleshoot it.
Thank you,
Dean

Hi Dean,

Thanks for the screenshot. What it shows is the Norn OS Network Configuration page with hostname DC08, the Wi-Fi Configuration tab selected, SSID and password both empty, protocol DHCP, and the Save and Restart buttons with the note that the device must be restarted after saving. One thing worth knowing straight away: those fields coming up empty after a reboot is not by itself proof that nothing was saved. Norn OS does not echo the stored password back into the form, and on 1.0.0 it often does not re-populate the SSID either. The only reliable evidence is whether the unit actually joins, which in your case it does not.

On the likely cause. The D.08's stock Hammer firmware uses an ESP32 radio, so it is 2.4 GHz only, and its Wi-Fi stack is stricter than the one in Harlo OS that your NerdQAxe++ and BC04 are running. Two routers broadcasting one network name is exactly the setup that trips it: if either router does band steering, or the SSID is also published on 5 GHz, or the security is WPA3 or WPA2/WPA3 mixed with protected management frames required, the DC08 will accept the credentials, fail the association on boot, and fall straight back to the setup AP and the QR screen. That is the same behaviour you are describing, and it explains why your other two miners are unaffected.

So here is the procedure I would use rather than the 192.168.4.1 portal. Plug Ethernet back in, open the miner's web interface at its LAN address, go to Network, Wi-Fi Configuration, and use the small magnifier button at the end of the SSID field to scan and pick your network from the list instead of typing it. That makes the firmware store the exact SSID and the band it actually sees. Enter the password, leave Protocol on DHCP, press SAVE, then press the RESTART button in the page rather than pulling the power, and give it two full minutes. Then unplug Ethernet and power cycle. If it comes up on Wi-Fi, you are done.

If it still falls back to the QR screen, do one decisive test before touching firmware. Put your phone into hotspot mode on 2.4 GHz with a short simple name, no spaces, WPA2, and a plain alphanumeric password, and point the DC08 at that. If it joins the hotspot, the unit and the firmware are fine and the problem is the router environment. The fix is then on the router side: create a separate 2.4 GHz only SSID with its own distinct name, WPA2-AES rather than WPA3 or mixed, management frame protection off or optional, band steering off, and let the DC08 use that one. Also worth checking that neither router has MAC filtering on or a full DHCP pool.

On your three questions. A reset is reasonable and harmless: do one factory reset from Settings before the hotspot test if saving keeps failing. A firmware update I cannot promise you, because I could not find any Norn OS release newer than the 1.0.0 dated 2026-09-12 that you have, and I will not guess at a version. A reflash I would not do yet, it is the step after the hotspot test, and only with Hammer's own image. Flashing Harlo OS to the spare LilyGo as you planned would also sidestep this entirely, since that is the stack already working on your other two miners, and your original board stays untouched.

What would help most if it does not clear: the Logs page contents cap····right after a save and a restart, especially the lines around the Wi-Fi connect attempt and any disconnect reason code, the exact version string from Settings, the make and model of both routers with the security mode and band shown for that SSID, and whether the SSID or password contains spaces or special characters. Please do not send me the password itself, just tell me its length and whether it has symbols.

I have passed this to JD, our hardware lead, to confirm whether the 1.0.0 provisioning path has a known bug and whether a newer DC08 build exists. The team picks it up Monday at 10am ET and the answer will come to you by email. If you want a faster read over the weekend, JD and a lot of DC08 owners are active in our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support
